item.title: Sal Salis Ningaloo Reef Reimagines Barefoot Luxury for 2027
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Sal Salis Ningaloo Reef is preparing to enter a new chapter, with a major refurbishment set to transform the eco-luxury camp before it reopens in late March 2027. Tucked among the dunes of Western Australia’s Cape Range National Park and just steps from the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Ningaloo Reef, the 16-tent retreat will introduce redesigned Wilderness Tents with private ensuite bathrooms, marine-inspired interiors and furnishings chosen to reflect the colors and textures of the surrounding coastline.

Designed by Woods Bagot, the refurbishment extends beyond the accommodations to reshape the guest experience throughout the camp. A refreshed reception will lead into a new central sundeck and lounge, creating a social heart for the property, while a new dining area with banquette seating and an all-inclusive open bar adds another gathering point. The culinary offering will also be refined around seasonal, locally sourced produce, with Western Australian wines and regional beers included. Guests will continue to explore the landscape through guided gorge walks, snorkeling, kayaking and stand-up paddleboarding, with optional whale shark and humpback whale swims offering encounters with Ningaloo’s marine life.

The Curated Take

Sal Salis has always made its setting the centerpiece of the stay, and the refurbishment appears designed to strengthen rather than compete with that proposition. Reclaimed timber, woven details and materials selected to weather naturally connect the interiors to the coastal environment, while the new communal spaces give guests more ways to gather between adventures. It is a thoughtful interpretation of barefoot luxury, where comfort is elevated without losing the sense that you are living lightly within a remarkable wilderness.

item.title: National Scenic Byway Day Invites Travelers to Rediscover America by Road
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
September 22 will mark the first annual National Scenic Byway Day, a new observance encouraging travelers to explore the scenic, historic and culturally significant roads that connect communities across the United States. The timing is particularly notable in 2026, which also marks the nation’s 250th birthday and the centennial of the U.S. Numbered Highway System. For travelers drawn to road trips, the day offers a reason to slow down, leave the major highways behind and experience the places and stories found along America’s scenic routes.

Among the country’s standout byways is the 444-mile Natchez Trace Parkway, stretching through Mississippi, Alabama and Tennessee. The route combines sweeping landscapes with archaeological sites, historic markers, recreational opportunities and access to small communities, tracing layers of history from Indigenous homelands and early travel routes to the modern road trip. Travelers can mark National Scenic Byway Day by planning a scenic drive, visiting a byway community, exploring local museums and historic sites, or building a longer itinerary around one of America’s designated scenic routes.

The Curated Take

There is something especially appealing about a travel day built around the idea that getting there can be part of the experience. Scenic byways offer a slower form of American travel, where landscapes, local history and small communities become part of the itinerary rather than scenery passed at highway speed. National Scenic Byway Day arrives as a timely invitation to rediscover that kind of journey.

item.title: Barcelona’s SIPS Brings Its World-Class Cocktail Culture to Las Vegas
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Caesars Palace is bringing a taste of Barcelona’s celebrated cocktail scene to Las Vegas this fall as SIPS Drinkery House takes over VISTA Cocktail Lounge from October 31 through December 31. Founded by bartenders Simone Caporale and Marc Álvarez, the Eixample bar was named The World’s Best Bar in 2023 by The World’s 50 Best Bars and has remained among the global top three in the two years since. Its limited-time Las Vegas residency coincides with Caesars Palace’s 60th anniversary.

SIPS is known for putting flavor and technique ahead of convention, pairing familiar ingredients with inventive preparation and playful presentation. At VISTA, guests will encounter signature creations including the Purple Rain, a contemporary take on a whiskey sour combining bourbon with wild sour honey and beetroot, and the Mosaic, which pairs pisco brandy with aromatic woods from the Amazon rainforest and arrives in a painted glass inspired by Barcelona’s modernist art movement. The collaboration offers a rare opportunity to experience the work of one of Barcelona’s most influential cocktail destinations without leaving the Strip.

The Curated Take

Las Vegas has long borrowed from the world’s great dining cities, but this collaboration feels particularly well suited to the city’s appetite for spectacle. SIPS brings something more interesting than a familiar European name: a distinct cocktail philosophy in which the drink itself remains the focus, while technique, glassware and presentation become part of the experience.

item.title: Four Seasons Resort Bali at Sayan Reframes the Riverside Suite Experience
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Four Seasons Resort Bali at Sayan has unveiled the first seven suites in its sustainability-led refresh, introducing five Premier Duplex Suites and two Premier Family Suites that bring a contemporary interpretation to the resort’s signature relationship with the Ayung River valley. Created with Hirsch Bedner Associates (HBA), the redesigned spaces pair floor-to-ceiling views with hand-loomed textiles, locally crafted details, natural materials and a refined residential feel. Pale, earthy tones echo Ubud’s rice terraces, while dark stained teak grounds the interiors and integrated smart technology remains intentionally unobtrusive.

The 85-square-metre Premier Duplex Suite unfolds across two levels, with a river-facing living and dining area, teak-and-textile bedroom and private sun terrace designed for lingering. The Premier Family Suite takes a more tailored approach to multigenerational stays, placing a dedicated children’s room at the center of the experience while giving parents a generous living space overlooking the valley. Sustainability is embedded in the renovation itself, with the existing framework refurbished rather than rebuilt, locally sourced materials selected for longevity where possible, and energy-efficient lighting and next-generation air conditioning incorporated into the design.

The Curated Take

Sayan’s appeal has always been rooted in the feeling of being immersed in the landscape rather than simply looking at it. These first reimagined suites build on that idea without abandoning the resort’s distinctive architecture or Balinese character. The result is less a wholesale reinvention than a considered evolution, with the river, craftsmanship and sense of place remaining the defining elements.

item.title: St. Augustine’s Nights of Lights Returns With a Smarter Way to Navigate the Celebration
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
St. Augustine’s Nights of Lights returns November 21, illuminating the historic city with more than 3 million lights through January 18, 2027. Along with the annual celebration, visitors will have an upgraded version of the free Nights of Lights app, which earned a Bronze Flagler Award for Websites at VISIT FLORIDA’s 2026 Flagler Awards after nearly 90,000 downloads during its first season. The app puts maps, parking, shuttle information, events and visitor tips in one place, helping travelers navigate one of Florida’s most popular holiday traditions.

For the 2026 season, the app adds a new search function for restaurants, attractions, events and live music, a visual display of parking availability and redesigned maps, with additional features expected in October. The festival itself begins with Light-Up! Night in the Plaza de la Constitución, where the city’s historic core is illuminated for the season. Visitors can also use the app to explore different ways of experiencing the lights, from boats and trolleys to helicopters and the St. Augustine Lighthouse, while extending their stay to explore the surrounding Florida’s Historic Coast.

The Curated Take

Nights of Lights is already a visual spectacle, but the practical reality of visiting a historic city during a major holiday event can be considerably less magical. The app addresses that gap by treating logistics as part of the travel experience, helping visitors figure out where to park, how to get around and what to do once they arrive. For travelers planning a holiday getaway rather than simply an evening visit, that ability to move beyond the lights and discover dining, attractions and experiences across St. Augustine makes the technology particularly useful.

item.title: Kuganha Brings Private In-Suite Wellness to the Western Cape Safari
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Kuganha has opened in South Africa’s Western Cape, introducing a new take on the luxury safari experience within a 10,000-hectare rewilded Big Five conservancy less than two and a half hours from Cape Town. Limited to just 10 private tented suites, each measuring at least 320 square metres, the property combines safari, conservation and an unusually comprehensive approach to private wellness, with the entire experience designed around each guest’s own pace.

Wellness is built directly into the suites, rather than confined to a traditional spa. Guests have access to private saunas, steam rooms, a Himalayan salt oxygen halotherapy room, flotation deprivation pods, ice plunge baths, jacuzzi plunge pools and double massage beds, along with an introductory wellness journey to guide them through the facilities. The culinary program follows the same personalized philosophy, with fresh, organic and locally sourced ingredients tailored around each guest’s wellness journey. Meals can be enjoyed privately or at the Kuganha restaurant overlooking the infinity pool, waterhole and surrounding Karoo landscape. Beyond the suites, the property’s rewilding story adds another dimension, with Big Five wildlife reintroduced to land where many species had disappeared centuries ago.

The Curated Take

Kuganha is tapping into an intriguing evolution in luxury wellness: the desire to retreat from the world without giving up the comforts, privacy or personalization of a high-end stay. Here, wellness is not a schedule of treatments guests move through during the day. It is embedded in the accommodation itself, then paired with wildlife, open landscapes and conservation. The result is a safari experience where the natural environment is not simply the backdrop, but part of the restorative proposition.

item.title: Four Seasons Bali Turns Movie Night Into a Quiet Cinema by the Sea
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Four Seasons Resort Bali at Jimbaran Bay is giving movie night a distinctly beachfront setting with the launch of Jimbaran Cinema, a “Quiet Cinema” experience at the resort’s secluded Coconut Grove. Running Sundays and Mondays from September 13 through November 9, the open-air screenings pair sunset drinks, relaxed beachfront dining and classic films with a headphone-based audio experience that leaves the sound of the waves undisturbed.

Guests settle into bean bags, sun beds or armchair sofas at 6 p.m. for a sunset drink before the film begins at 7:30 p.m. Using CineWav, the movie soundtrack is streamed directly to guests’ mobile phones through their own earphones, creating a more intimate viewing experience. Sunday screenings are geared toward families and friends with films including Mamma Mia! and The Greatest Showman, while Mondays take a more romantic turn with titles such as The Notebook. In-seat service continues throughout the film, with popcorn, soft drinks and juice included, alongside a menu of elevated cinema snacks such as lobster rolls, coconut crab nachos, Korean-style fried chicken and truffle parmesan fries.

The Curated Take

The cleverness of Jimbaran Cinema is that the technology is designed to make the setting quieter, not louder. By keeping the soundtrack in guests’ ears, the experience preserves the natural soundscape of Jimbaran Bay while transforming the beach into a private-feeling cinema beneath the stars. It is a simple idea, but one that feels particularly well suited to Bali, where the environment is as much a part of the evening as the movie itself.

item.title: Kandooma Maldives Reimagines the Island Experience Beyond the Rebrand
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
When Holiday Inn Resort Kandooma Maldives becomes Kandooma Maldives on October 1, the change will represent far more than a new name. The South Malé Atoll resort is using the transition to reshape its guest experience, with refreshed and new dining and leisure concepts, additional accommodation options, upgraded villas and a new approach to All-Inclusive built around the experiences travelers come to the Maldives to enjoy.

The resort is organizing its new identity around five signatures: Kandooma Blue, Kandooma Flow, Kandooma Table, Kandooma Social and Kandooma Ways, encompassing ocean experiences, movement and wellbeing, food, social connection and opportunities to discover Maldivian island life. Diving, surfing and watersports remain central, while the resort is expanding its land-based activities and offerings for families and teenagers. A new Kandooma Beach Club is also planned, alongside a phased refurbishment of villas and public spaces. Once the transformation is complete, the resort will offer 146 villas, including new two-bedroom accommodations.

The Curated Take

The more interesting part of Kandooma’s rebrand is its philosophy that All-Inclusive should be measured in memories rather than meals. By making activities such as scuba diving part of the proposition and building the brand around the island itself, Kandooma is positioning the resort as an experience to participate in rather than simply a place to stay. For a destination where many resorts can begin to blur together, that focus on what makes one particular island distinctive could be the more meaningful transformation.

item.title: China Moves Onto the Wish Lists of Younger Travelers
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
China may be poised for a bigger role in the young-traveler market. A 12-month poll of 13,256 INTRO Travel customers found that more than one in five named China among their top choices for a future trip, prompting the group tour operator to develop its first China program for travelers ages 18 to 40. The two proposed itineraries combine major cultural landmarks with destinations that have become increasingly visible on social media, including Zhangjiajie, Chengdu and Chongqing.

The 12-day China Express travels from Shanghai through Zhangjiajie, Chengdu, Xi’an, Luoyang and Dengfeng before reaching Beijing, while the 17-day China Adventure begins in Hong Kong and adds Yangshuo, Chongqing and Shanghai. Both include major draws such as the Great Wall, Terracotta Army and Forbidden City, with high-speed rail connecting much of the journey. Groups will be capped at 16, with the format designed to ease some of the practical challenges first-time visitors can face, from transportation and payments to navigating a country where independent travel can require more preparation.

The Curated Take

China has long had the cultural depth to appeal to adventurous travelers, but it has not carried the same easy familiarity among younger Western travelers as Thailand, Bali or Japan. That may be changing. Greater visa accessibility for some travelers, growing social-media visibility and the appeal of seeing somewhere that still feels less predictable could give China a new position in the young-traveler landscape. INTRO’s approach is particularly telling: rather than treating China as a complicated destination to conquer independently, it packages the logistical complexity into a social, fast-moving group journey.
